source: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
summary: Builds replayable episodic memory for agents from execution traces; only keeps a run as a memory episode if an evaluator passes. Addresses cross-run learning for agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to HID-188 (inject cross-run episodic memory into planner/executor prompts); no new issue needed as the theme is already tracked.

source: TraceBrain: An Open-Source Framework for Agentic Trace Management (IJCAI 2026)
summary: OpenTelemetry-based infrastructure for storing and retrieving past agent execution history. More of an observability and governance layer than a memory system.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — could complement HID-163 observability work, but AgentForge's current gap is telemetry data collection, not a retrieval framework for traces.

summary: MIT-licensed self-improving coding and research harness released August 2026. Uses a persistent IPython kernel and append-only JSONL session history. Self-refines within the same reasoning session.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting but AgentForge's sequential determinism is a design choice; self-modification of prompts/loops is a red flag (prompt self-evolution pattern from 2026 noise audit).

source: A Self-Improving Coding Agent (Robeyns, Szummer, Aitchison; arXiv 2504.15228)
summary: NeurIPS 2025 submission: agent autonomously edits itself and improves performance on SWE Bench Verified from 17% to 53%. Mechanism is LLM reflection plus code updates.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — foundational paper for self-improvement; the partial retry theme (HID-186) is a more grounded, incremental step toward this; full self-modification is premature for AgentForge.

summary: LangGraph 1.2.16 and @langchain/langgraph 1.5.1 current as of Oct 2026. Added per-call approvals, built-in MCP, node timeouts, DeltaChannel for cheaper long threads.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses, not LangGraph state machines; DeltaChannel and built-in MCP are LangGraph-specific and don't transfer to AgentForge's architecture.

source: Towards Budget-Aware Agents: Can LLM Agents Know What They Will Spend? (ICML 2026)
summary: ICML 2026 paper evaluating five frontier models on token, cost, and time budgets. Finds budget awareness decouples from task performance and is actionable as a control signal.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to HID-163 (token cost and stage latency telemetry with budget enforcement); no new issue needed as that theme is already in backlog.

summary: Karpathy framing of 'agentic engineering' where the human orchestrates agents as oversight. Describes a programmable layer of abstraction: agents, subagents, prompts, contexts, memory, tools, skills, hooks, MCP.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptual framing that validates AgentForge's existing architecture; no new technical gap identified from this source.

summary: CrewAI at 1.15.18 (Aug 2026) with Crew Studio Flow construction; AutoGen moved to maintenance mode, replaced by Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (April 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI-subprocess model, not these frameworks; no transferable patterns identified beyond what is already implemented.

source: INTENT: Budget Feasibility for LLM Agents (arXiv 2602.11541, Feb 2026)
summary: Finds standalone agents frequently violate hard budget constraints; prompt-based cost feedback is insufficient. Proposes lightweight online planning framework to maintain budget feasibility.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — supports the need for HID-163 (cost telemetry); budget feasibility planning is in scope of that issue, not a new gap.

source: EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective (arXiv 2605.18421)
summary: Benchmark framework for evaluating cross-episode execution learning in agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — evaluation benchmark infrastructure, not an implementation pattern applicable to AgentForge's current needs.
